## Overview Fixes #59887. `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (added in #54049) passes `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to FlashInfer's CuTeDSL MegaMoE config. The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 calls that field `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, so the backend raises `TypeError` while the layer is built. This PR drops the kwarg and adds a regression test that doesn't need SM100. `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` is unaffected. ## Claims - With the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` no longer raises `TypeError` when the layer is built. Behavior is as intended: `False` is the field's default in every FlashInfer release from v0.7.0 through v0.7.1. - The fix doesn't depend on the FlashInfer version: 0.7.1 (released 2026-10-09; #60948 bumps the pin) renames the field but keeps its `False` default, and the new test passes against 0.7.1's config types (constructor check only; the backend itself was not run on 0.7.1). With 0.7.1, `main`'s current kwarg becomes valid too; this PR keeps 0.7.0.x working and adds the drift test. - On 4× GB200 at current `main`, with `nvshmem4py` installed and #61041's decoder-replay fix copied in, the backend serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with default CUDA graphs (FULL and PIECEWISE captured). GSM8K is 0.891 (one run), vs 0.901 for `deep_gemm_mega_moe` and 0.910 for the default MoE backend on the same image. - New test `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer`: it builds the adapter against the installed FlashInfer's real config types, without SM100 or multiple GPUs (it also passes with no GPU visible). It lives in `tests/kernels/moe`, which the L4 `kernels-moe-test` job runs; no Buildkite job has run on this PR yet. - **What it catches:** a renamed or removed kwarg in FlashInfer's MoE-EP config types, or removal of the deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases. Before, these only failed at model load on SM100. - **What it doesn't cover:** `MoEEpTensors` and the megakernel layer's own methods. Only the SM100 e2e test covers those. ## Validation ### Retest at current `main` (3c062d391d) `main` was merged into this branch (no conflicts); the PR still changes only `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` (the kwarg) and its test. All runs were on 4× GB200 (docker, with the Slurm job's IMEX channel) in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` arm64 `sha256:f853a683…`, built from 7d0b4e57aa. That image's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and `vllm/config/kernel.py` are identical to `main`'s. - **base:** the image as is. - **fix:** the image with this PR's `flashinfer_moe_ep.py` copied over the installed one. - Tests ran from this branch's `tests/` tree. The CuTeDSL path also needs `nvshmem4py` (#59903, installed by #59912), so `nvshmem4py-cu13` (0.4.0) was installed in the container. | Check | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer` | `[cutedsl]` ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'`; `[deep_gemm]` ✅ | ✅ 2/2; also 2/2 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` | | Same, with `flashinfer-python==0.7.1` installed (constructor check only; run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`, and with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` because the image's `flashinfer-cubin` is 0.7.0.post1) | ✅ 2/2 | ✅ 2/2 | | `pytest kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k "test_init_warmup and cutedsl"` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` (ran the 2-GPU dsv4-flash case) | ✅ 8/8, run twice | | DEP=4 serve, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, default CUDA graphs | all 4 DP ranks raise the same `TypeError` right after the checkpoint loads; the server exits about 2 minutes in | serves (FULL and PIECEWISE graphs captured); answers correct; GSM8K **0.891** | - **Serve command:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` (revision `2cba9e42`, pre-downloaded; containers run with `--ipc=host` so the DP replicas share the Engram tables through `/dev/shm`). Startup takes about 10 minutes, which can exceed the default 600 s engine-ready timeout. - **GSM8K:** `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 128`, one run. For reference, on the same image the default MoE backend scored 0.910 and `deep_gemm_mega_moe` 0.901 (#61041's validation). One run's standard error is about 0.008 (about 0.012 for a two-run difference), so the gap to the default is about 1.6 SE; other runs of this backend scored 0.888–0.899 (#59912's retest, #61041). The fix run also had #61041's one-file decoder-replay fix copied in: without it, every FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load on current `main` (#61040), independent of this PR. - **Also covered:** #59912's retest, on images built from `main` c41b2639e2 + #59912 + this PR, passed the kwargs test (2/2) and the CuTeDSL e2e tests (8/8) on GB200, GB300 and B200, and, with the same decoder-replay fix, served DEP=4/8/16 with GSM8K 0.888–0.897. - **pre-commit:** `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/flashinfer_moe_ep.py` passes. - **pytest:** run from `tests/` with `-v -rs --timeout=900`.
Earlier validation (at 7712663, on main 84bcbc6264; locally built images) All runs were on 4× GB200. Images were built from `docker/Dockerfile` with the arm64 CI build args, with these deviations: `torch_cuda_arch_list=10.0`, no sccache, `RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false`, local `max_jobs`/`nvcc_threads`, and an added `vllm-openai` target. **fix** from this branch at 7712663 (35b3ca5 only edits a comment and docstrings), **base** from `main` @ 84bcbc6264. | Test | base (main) | fix | |---|---|---| | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[cutedsl]` | ❌ `TypeError: Sm100_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce'` | ✅ | | `test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer[deep_gemm]` | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs[*-cutedsl-*]` (2 and 4 GPUs, 4 geometries) | ❌ same `TypeError` in every worker | ✅ 8/8 (one case hung once and passed on retry) | Serving DEP=4: base, with the default cudagraph mode, crashed on every DP rank with the `TypeError` before graph capture. Fix, with `--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (full-graph capture failed in that environment), served, answered correctly, and scored GSM8K 0.898 (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`) vs 0.901 for the default backend with the same flag. `nvshmem4py-cu13==0.4.0` was installed in a test-only layer, and containers got the Slurm job's IMEX channel (without it NVSHMEM's fabric `cuMemCreate` fails with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`).
## Details **Root cause.** FlashInfer renamed `in_kernel_fc2_reduce` to `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce` in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4604, first shipped in v0.7.1rc1 and now in v0.7.1. The adapter was written against the new name while vLLM still pins 0.7.0.post1 (`requirements/cuda.txt`). Every other kwarg and method the adapter uses on FlashInfer's MoE-EP types is present in both 0.7.0.post1 and 0.7.1, so this was the only mismatch. **Why CI missed it.** The only test that constructs the adapter, `test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, needs SM100 and 2+ GPUs. `kernels-moe-test` runs on L4, so it always skips there, and no B200 job runs this file. The new test fakes four things: - `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer`, which allocates symmetric memory; - the EP group; - the device index; - `_expose_deep_gemm_to_flashinfer`, which imports DeepGEMM. Everything FlashInfer receives is its own config dataclasses plus a real `MoEWeightPack`. **Relation to #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1).** #60948 bumps the pin to 0.7.1 and doesn't touch `flashinfer_moe_ep.py`; the two PRs don't conflict and pass in either order. After #60948, `main`'s explicit `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=False` would be valid; dropping it still gives the same `False` default (0.7.1 documents the flag as an opt-in to nondeterministic accumulation), keeps the backend working on 0.7.0.x, and the new test guards both versions. **Alternatives considered.** *Version-gate the kwarg name:* unnecessary, since the value equals the default. **Related, found while validating.** - **`nvshmem4py` packaging:** vLLM's images don't ship `nvshmem4py`, so without it `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` fails at FlashInfer's runtime bootstrap. Tracked in #59903, fixed by #59912. - **Decoder replay under load:** on current `main`, DeepSeek-V4.1 with either FlashInfer MegaMoE backend crashes under GSM8K load in the decoder-replay CUDA graph. Tracked in #61040, fixed by #61041. - **Earlier limitations that no longer reproduce at current `main`:** full CUDA-graph capture with this backend (FULL graphs captured above), and the DeepGEMM "type Runtime is already registered" import error (#59904; the vendored DeepGEMM moved to `TORCH_LIBRARY` in #48962). The one-off 2-GPU e2e hang did not recur in 16 cases. - The adapter still imports FlashInfer's deprecated `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig`/`DeepGemmMegaMoeConfig` aliases, which FlashInfer has scheduled for removal. Switching to the `Sm100_*` names is a follow-up; the new test would flag the removal. **Duplicate check.** Apart from #59887, which I filed for this bug, no open or closed issue or PR mentions `enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `in_kernel_fc2_reduce`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` or `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig` as a fix for it. #60948 (FlashInfer 0.7.1 bump) makes `main`'s kwarg valid but leaves 0.7.0.x broken and adds no test. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

@@ -10,9 +10,14 @@
 the DeepGEMM kernel (FP8 activations and FP4 weights, power-of-two scales per
 32). The expected output is then known in closed form and compared bit for
 bit.
+
+A test that needs no SM100 also checks the adapter's kwargs against the
+installed FlashInfer's config types, so config drift fails on any CI runner
+with FlashInfer installed.
 """
 
 from dataclasses import dataclass
+from types import SimpleNamespace
 
 import pytest
 import torch
@@ -22,6 +27,7 @@
 from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
 from vllm.config.kernel import FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL, FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_DEEP_GEMM
 from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import ensure_model_parallel_initialized
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import flashinfer_moe_ep as fi_ep
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
     FusedMoEConfig,
@@ -305,3 +311,59 @@ def test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs(
     if torch.accelerator.device_count() < world_size:
         pytest.skip(f"Need at least {world_size} GPUs")
     distributed_run(_init_warmup_forward, world_size, geometry, backend)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", BACKENDS, ids=("cutedsl", "deep_gemm"))
+def test_adapter_kwargs_match_installed_flashinfer(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, backend: str
+):
+    """The adapter's kwargs construct the installed FlashInfer's config types.
+
+    Needs no SM100, so config kwarg drift fails in CI rather than at model load.
+    Fakes only the megakernel layer (symmetric memory), the EP group, the device
+    index and the DeepGEMM import.
+    """
+    moe_ep = pytest.importorskip("flashinfer.moe_ep")
+    layer_args: list[tuple] = []
+
+    class FakeMegaLayer:
+        def __init__(self, *args) -> None:
